description: Build the fully styled individual species page template with all content sections rendered from the JSON data files, maintaining the liquid-glass aesthetic and including TMDB media display, accessibility features, and proper SEO markup.
steps: Flesh out src/species-page.js to be a complete, working species page renderer that: (a) reads the slug from the page's data attribute or URL path, (b) fetches public/data/{slug}.json, (c) renders all sections into the page: hero with species name/scientific name/conservation status badge and a key stat, habitat section with glass-panel, TMDB media section showing film/documentary cards with poster images (use TMDB image base URL https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w300), threats section, conservation status section, cultural significance section, (d) adds breadcrumb navigation at the top (Observatory > Species Name), (e) initializes GSAP scroll animations for the species page sections

Create src/species-page.css with styles specific to species pages: media card grid (poster + title + year + rating), hero section with large species name, section layouts. Reuse glass-panel/glass-card patterns from style.css. Import this CSS in species-page.js

Ensure each species HTML template (species/*.html) has: skip-to-content link, proper lang attribute, viewport meta, canonical URL, Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:image using a placeholder or TMDB backdrop), JSON-LD with @type: 'WebPage' and about: @type 'Animal' with species info, link to the shared species-page.js and species-page.css
Add a back-to-observatory link/button in the breadcrumb that navigates to the index page
Handle the case where TMDB media array is empty gracefully (show a message like 'No films or documentaries found yet')
Ensure poster images have alt text (film title), and the media section has proper heading hierarchy
Add a simple footer to species pages consistent with the vision section footer style
Verify all 10 species pages render correctly by confirming build succeeds and the dist output contains properly bundled species pages
acceptance_criteria: Each species page renders hero, habitat, media, threats, conservation, and cultural significance sections from JSON data
TMDB media cards display poster images, titles, release years, and ratings where available
Breadcrumb navigation appears on all species pages with link back to main observatory
JSON-LD structured data is present in each species page HTML
npm run build succeeds and dist/species/*.html files are complete with bundled JS/CSS
Species pages maintain the liquid-glass pastel aesthetic consistent with the main page
Accessibility: skip links, proper heading hierarchy (h1 > h2 > h3), alt text on images, ARIA labels on interactive elements
verification: Run 'npm run build' and confirm it succeeds
Check that dist/species/tiger.html includes bundled CSS and JS references
Verify the build output size is reasonable (species pages should share chunks)
